exposure: larger gaps between marriage and childbirth
cohort: The study included 486 women with histopathologically confirmed breast cancer (246 HR+, 240 TNBC) and 443 cancer-free women from a tertiary hospital in Bangladesh.
finding: Using machine learning, the study identified context-specific socio-demographic and reproductive factors, such as rural residence, low education, and undernutrition, as predictors for breast cancer subtypes in Bangladesh, with Cesarean delivery being more predictive of TNBC.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was found to be more predictive of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) compared to hormone-receptor-positive (HR+) breast cancer.
